Findings below — one important correction to the task premise discovered en route: **fontanf's repo is no longer branch-and-bound**; its current main branch ships only MILP + Bellman DP (the Dyer–Zemel file is an empty 0-byte stub).

## google/or-tools — `knapsack_solver.{h,cc}`
URLs: https://github.com/google/or-tools/blob/stable/ortools/algorithms/knapsack_solver.h · https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google/or-tools/stable/ortools/algorithms/knapsack_solver.cc
- Per-dimension `KnapsackCapacityPropagator` (one per capacity), each with its own efficiency-sorted item list | bounds computed independently, no shared mutable state; `IncrementalUpdate` applies/reverts one assignment to ALL propagators and never stops on failure so state stays consistent/incremental | yes | model each constraint (here: 1) as a tiny propagator object holding `consumed_capacity`, `current_profit`, preallocated `Float64Array`-style sorted arrays.
- Bounds: greedy fill in efficiency order over unbound items → **lower bound + greedy solution snapshot**; upper bound = break-item LP-ish extra via `max(remaining_cap·next_profit/next_weight, break_profit − overused_cap·prev_profit/prev_weight)` in exact int arithmetic (`UpperBoundOfRatio`, overflow-checked; double fallback only if MSB sum > 61) | integer-safe bound keeps search deterministic and prune-tight | yes | port as `(rem*p + w - 1) / w` with `Math.trunc`; keep integers, no floats.
- Multidim aggregation = **min of all propagators' upper bounds** (`GetAggregatedProfitUpperBound`); branch item = first unbound item in *primary* propagator's sort (can pick most-constrained dimension; header TODO notes Dobson aggregated efficiency as unimplemented) | cheap, valid composite bound | yes (trivial with 1 dim) | if we ever add a second budget (e.g., cost), just min the two bounds.
- Search: best-first `priority_queue` on upper bound, **tie-break to higher current profit** ("usually closer to a leaf… smaller path"); early exit `while queue nonempty && top.UB > best_profit`; `MakeNewNode` computes bounds on a scratch node and discards before heap allocation | prunes before allocating; dives to good incumbents fast | only-for-large-instances | our instances likely never need B&B over DP; keep as fallback.
- **Reduction pass in the wrapper** (`use_reduction_`): for each item compute forced-out/in upper bounds via `GetLowerAndUpperBoundWhenItem`, fix items where best lower bound exceeds them; if all items fixed, returns without any search, else builds a reduced instance with adjusted capacities | solves easy instances outright | yes | per-group: drop dominated options (weight↑ & profit↓) — even cheaper than or-tools' bound fixing.
- `Knapsack64ItemsSolver`: uint64 bitmask DFS, precomputed **prefix sums of profits/weights over efficiency-sorted items**, break item by `upper_bound` binary search on prefix weights, incremental `state_weight_`/`rejected_items_profit_` on backtrack; ~4× faster than generic B&B; measured notes in comments: bound caching not worth it (1/7 reuse), O(depth) incremental loop beat O(1) prefix arithmetic by 10% in C++ | flat prefix arrays make bounds O(log n) per node | only-for-large-instances (JS lacks cheap 64-bit bitmask state; BigInt too slow) | keep prefix-sum idea, skip bitmask.
- `KnapsackBruteForceSolver` (≤30 items): iterates all 2ⁿ states via **XOR of adjacent states → update only changed bits' sums**; interleaved `profits_weights_[2*i]` flat array | cache-friendly, incremental sums | no | only relevant below ~20 options total.
- DP solver: 1-D `computed_profits_` array, descending capacity loop (no 2-D table); solution reconstructed by **re-solving on the residual** (`num_items = selected_item_id`) instead of storing parents; D&C solver = Kellerer/Pferschy/Pisinger DP-2: O(cap·n) time, O(cap+n) space via two rolling arrays | minimal allocation | yes | the re-solve trick removes the parent table entirely.

## fontanf/multiplechoiceknapsacksolver
URL: https://github.com/fontanf/multiplechoiceknapsacksolver (+ https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fontanf/multiplechoiceknapsacksolver/main/src/algorithms/dynamic_programming_bellman.cpp)
- **Correction: no B&B exists on main** — README lists only MILP, MILP linear-relaxation, and DP; `dyer_zemel.cpp` (convex-hull/LP route) is an empty 0-byte stub per the git tree API | — | — | don't cite it as a B&B reference.
- Two-row Bellman DP (`values_prev`/`values_next`, each `capacity+1`) over groups; per group only iterate weights in **[weight_min, min(capacity, weight_sum)]** where `weight_sum` += per-group max item weight | prunes unreachable states; exact | **yes — this is our exact problem shape** | `Int32Array(cap+1)` ×2, swap refs not copy; inner loop `for w desc, for option: next[w]=max(next[w], prev[w-wj]+pj)`.
- "-all" variant stores full (groups+1)×(cap+1) table with `state_id=(g+1)*(cap+1)+w` and backtracks | enables solution recovery | yes | at ≤100 groups × token caps this fits easily; alternatively use or-tools' re-solve trick to skip it.

URL: https://github.com/jmyrberg/mknapsack
- Wraps Martello–Toth Fortran 77 classics: MT1/MT2/MT1R (0-1, MT1R = real inputs), MTB2, MTU1/MTU2, MTM/MTHM (multiple knapsacks), MTC2/MTCB, MTG/MTHG, MTP, MTSL | speed delegates entirely to compiled 1990 B&B Fortran; README carries **no performance notes**, and no MCKP routine exists | no | nothing in-loop; only the names are useful literature pointers.

## podkop/MO-MC-knapsack
URL: https://github.com/podkop/MO-MC-knapsack
- Multi-objective MCKP via scalarization (weighted sum, ε-constraint, ASF with `_rho=1e-4`) over CBC/Gurobi MILP; auto-creates per-class `Σx=1` constraints, supports non-rectangular classes, **normalizes coefficients to avoid numerical issues** | delegates everything to MILP engines | no (MILP in-loop unacceptable) | the only portable crumb: normalize coefficients — for us, keep integers instead.

## Top 5 most portable tricks, ranked
1. **Two-row Int32Array Bellman DP per group with reachable-weight windowing** (fontanf) — exact, deterministic, allocation-free after setup; comfortably sub-ms for 100 groups × 6 options.
2. **Greedy-break incumbent from efficiency order** (or-tools propagator) — free lower bound + feasible solution at every node; for MCKP, per-group greedy by profit/weight with the first-fit break gives an instant incumbent.
3. **Integer-arithmetic ratio upper bound at the break item** (or-tools `GetAdditionalProfit`) — `(rem*p)/w` and the symmetric overuse form, exact ints, overflow-checked; deterministic pruning with zero float drift.
4. **Prefix sums of sorted profits/weights + binary-search break item** (or-tools 64Items) — O(log n) bounds per node from two flat typed arrays.
5. **Bound-based reduction/fixing before search + per-group dominance prefilter** (or-tools wrapper) — fix or drop options before DP; at 1–6 options/group, pairwise dominance alone often shrinks instances dramatically.

**What I did:** fetched all 5 sources via web_extract (GitHub HTML, raw files, docs page, git-tree API), paged the 1460-line or-tools implementation from the local cache file, and cross-checked fontanf's actual source tree. **No files created or modified**; no issues besides the fontanf premise correction above.
